# Strategy A notes: Momentum

## Entry rules
- Buy names with positive 20-day AND 60-day returns that trade above their 50-day average.
- Rank by 60-day trend first and 20-day second. The 60d leader (PLTR) was the main pick in week 1. Keep doing this.
- Don't chase a single-day spike of more than 5%.
- If a name is more than 15% above its 50d average, treat it as extended: give it the smallest position or skip it.

## Sizing
- Hold 2-4 positions. Three positions was fine in week 1.
- Keep about $15-25 in cash so a rotation can happen without selling first.
- Use confidence 5-6 for ordinary momentum setups. Save 7+ for a name that leads on both 20d and 60d, is not extended, and has no spike. So far confidence has not predicted results (tournament: 1-4 avg +0.17%, 5-7 avg +0.13%, n=5), so don't raise it without a clear reason.

## Exits and rotation
- Rotate out when a holding falls below its 50d average, or when its 20d return turns negative and it drops out of the top momentum names.
- Hold a position at least 3 trading days unless it breaks its 50d average. Spread costs ($0.92 so far, about 0.18% of capital) are as large as our lead over SPY. Avoid churning.
- Make at most one rotation per day, and only when the replacement clearly ranks higher.

## Execution
- Place limit buys near the current ask, not far below it. All three fills came within about 0.3% of the limit.
- Check fills against the limit price. META was logged filling at 722.34 against a 720 limit, which should not happen with a buy limit. Report it if it happens again.

## Status after week 1
- Since start: +0.33% vs SPY +0.41%. Still behind. Week 1 was +1.35% vs +0.68%.
- Holding PLTR, META, AMD. AMD is the most extended. Cut it first if any weakness shows.

# Strategy B notes: Mean reversion

## Entry setup (unchanged core)
- Look for liquid names with a sharp 5-day drop that is large for their volatility (roughly 2x normal 5-day move or more), while the 60-day trend is still intact and price is near or above its 50d MA.
- Skip drops caused by clear bad news: earnings misses, guidance cuts, sector-wide regulatory or pricing shocks (e.g. the VZ/T one-day -8% on 10/09).
- An unexplained sharp drop is not an automatic skip. Before deciding, check for news. If none turns up and the trend is intact, it can be a small position.

## Sizing and cash
- Sitting almost all in cash guarantees lagging SPY in an up week (this week: +0.14% vs SPY +0.68%). Aim for 2-4 small positions in different, uncorrelated dips rather than one starter plus cash.
- Size by setup quality. A low-confidence starter is fine, but don't let one tiny position be the whole book week after week.
- Spread costs are large compared with these tiny positions ($1.96 paid so far vs a ~$72 position). Prefer names with tight spreads, avoid many tiny trades, and don't trade in and out.

## Orders
- Set limit prices near the current price. A limit far below the market either doesn't fill or fills at a very different price. Check the fill price against the limit after every fill. The CRM buy was placed @222.5 but filled @228.72, which is above the limit and looks like a data or execution anomaly; flag any repeat.

## Exits
- Take profits when the price gets back to about the pre-drop level (for CRM, roughly a 5% bounce from the low).
- Cut if the price falls about 5% below the entry/fill price, or if bad news comes out after entry.
- Time stop: if there's no bounce within about 10 trading days, exit and recycle the cash.

## Confidence
- Only one fill so far (conf 3), so there isn't enough data to judge calibration yet. Keep confidence honest; don't inflate it to get bigger size.
notes.C:
# Strategy C notes: Catalyst reader

## Identity
Trade only when a specific headline explains a price move or a lack of one. Look for over- and under-reactions. Holding cash is allowed, but cash has lagged SPY. Too much caution is a cost too.

## Entry rules
- Each session, look for the single best catalyst setup. Count it as a candidate if any of these apply:
  1. Large move (>5%) on news that is speculative, long-dated, or narrative-driven, e.g. "competitor might disrupt in years". This is a possible overreaction. Consider a small buy once the selling slows, e.g. the stock holds above its intraday low or bounces on day 2.
  2. Concrete, material news (earnings beat, guidance raise, contract, approval) with less than a 1% move. This is a possible underreaction.
- "I don't have an edge" is not a reason to skip a setup that matches 1 or 2. Write down why it's a mispricing or why it isn't, then decide.
- Don't buy into a fresh structural downtrend (e.g. a regulatory change or a guidance cut). Real fundamental damage is not an overreaction.

## Data hygiene
- If every price shows 0.0%, treat the data as stale. Hold, and say so in the journal. Don't count it as "no opportunity".

## Sizing and confidence
- Starter positions: confidence 5–6 and small size. Add only if the thesis is confirmed. So far, low and mid confidence buys across the tournament have been slightly positive (n=5, too small to tell much). No evidence yet supports using 8+.
- Hold at most 2 catalyst positions at a time.

## Exits
- Exit within 1–3 days, or once the catalyst looks priced in (e.g. about half the overreaction has been retraced).
- Exit right away if follow-up news confirms the move was justified.

## Log
- Week 1: 0 trades, 0.00% vs SPY +0.68%. Skipped the T/VZ selloff on SpaceX fears (-8–9%). That was a textbook case of rule 1 and should at least have been evaluated properly.
notes.D:
# Strategy D notes: Small-cap explorer

Identity: find tradable small-cap opportunities that SPY doesn't capture. Sitting in cash means we lose to SPY whenever the market rises (week 1: 0.00% vs SPY +0.68%). Being careful is fine, but holding cash forever is not a strategy.

## Screening (do this before deciding "hold")
- Ignore warrants (W/WS), units (U), rights (R) and anything under ~$0.50 straight away. Don't let them fill up the review.
- If the top-% mover list is all junk, look further down: small caps up or down 3–15% with real volume (a 1%-of-volume cap still large enough for our position size) and spreads ≤1–2%.
- Prefer: a second day of follow-through after a news catalyst (earnings, FDA, contract), pullbacks to support in names that already made a clean move, and sector moves where several small caps are rising together.
- Avoid chasing one-day spikes of +30% or more. Skipping VEEA at +51% was the right call.

## Entry and sizing
- When a liquid name passes the screen with a plausible 3–5x-spread move, take a small starter position (confidence 5–6) rather than holding.
- Aim for at least one well-reasoned position on most weeks. Keep 2–3 positions max, so that no single name dominates.
- Use limit orders at or near the mid. If the order doesn't fill, let it go rather than chasing.
- Avoid spreads wider than ~3%. Prefer spreads under 1.5%.

## Exits
- Decide the exit before buying: take profit at about 2–3x the expected-move target, and cut if the setup's thesis breaks (for example, the catalyst is faded and the stock falls back below the breakout level).
- Don't hold through a big binary event unless that event is the thesis.

## Confidence
- No data yet. Tournament-wide, 1–7 confidence buys have been slightly positive. Use 5–6 for normal setups and save 8+ for clear catalyst plus liquidity plus a clean chart.
notes.E:
# Strategy E: Claude's pick: Large-cap momentum, fully invested, low turnover

## Approach
Hold 3-4 liquid large-cap momentum leaders, or sector ETFs, that are in rising trends. To beat SPY, the money has to be invested. Sitting in cash is a guaranteed loss against SPY in an up week. Trade rarely, but get the orders filled.

## Universe
- US stocks over $10B market cap with average daily volume over $50M, or liquid ETFs (QQQ, XLK, SMH, XLF, XLI).
- Ignore small caps and penny stocks. Skip anything up more than 15% in 3 days.

## Entry
- Pick from the momentum-leaders list. Price must be above the 50-day average, and the 50-day must be above the 200-day.
- **Fills matter more than a few cents.** Set the limit at the last price or up to 0.3% above it. Don't bid under the market on a stock that's rising. If an order expires, re-place it at the last price at the next check-in. Don't chase more than one expiry.
- Prefer flat or pullback days, but don't wait more than one check-in for a pullback.
- Don't open a position within 2 days of earnings.
- If SPY is below its 50-day average or there's a broad selloff, hold at most 2 positions plus cash.

## Sizing
- Target: 3-4 positions with total cash at 10% or less by the end of the first check-in each week.
- Confidence 8 or higher gets a full slot (25-33%), 6-7 gets about two-thirds, 5 or lower means skip.
- **Cash sweep:** if more than 20% is still in cash after the stock picks (for example, because two-thirds slots leave a gap), put the remainder in QQQ or XLK as a core holding if allowed. Sell the sweep to fund a new leader.
- No more than 2 single stocks in the same sector (the sweep ETF doesn't count).

## Exits
- Sell if a position closes 8% below entry or below its 50-day average.
- Rotate only if a name falls off the leaders list AND a clearly stronger candidate exists. At most one rotation per slot per week.
- Trim half if a position is up 20% or more within 2 weeks.
- Ignore single red days or headlines that don't change the fundamentals.

## Habits
- Current holdings: META (about 32% of equity). Priority now: fill a second leader (MSFT if it still qualifies) and sweep the leftover cash.
- Default after the book is built: do nothing. Aim for 2-6 trades per week.
- Log a confidence score and a one-line reason for every trade.
